title: Kaurava Kunda Betta
tagline: Bengaluru → Devanahalli → Chikkaballapur → Kaurava Kunda. ~70 km, a granite twin hill near Isha Adiyogi with a short scramble to a 360° summit.
summary: An easy NH 44 run north past Devanahalli and the Nandi Hills turn-off brings you to Kaurava Kunda, a rocky twin hill off the Isha Adiyogi road near Chikkaballapur. Local lore ties the twin peaks to the Kauravas and Pandavas of the Mahabharata. A path of sandy steps climbs to a small Shiva temple partway up, then granite slabs and scrub lead to an open summit plateau with views over Nandi Hills, Skandagiri and the Chikkaballapur plains. Riders have pushed ADV bikes onto the rock, but most people park at the base and walk.

segments.note: City exit and the fast, wide airport highway past Kempegowda Airport to Devanahalli.
Four-lane highway past the Nandi Hills turn-off to Chikkaballapur.
~10 km of smaller roads towards Isha Adiyogi; the last stretch to the trailhead is a village track.

highlights: Twin granite peaks tied by local legend to the Kauravas and Pandavas
Small Shiva temple and mantapa partway up the hill
360° summit plateau looking over Nandi Hills, Skandagiri and the Chikkaballapur plains
Pairs well with the 112 ft Adiyogi bust at Sadhguru Sannidhi, Avalagurki, a few km away

offroad.summary: The ride is paved almost to the base; the off-road part is the rock itself, which most riders walk rather than ride.
notes: Approach to the trailhead is a short village track
Upper hill is open granite slab with loose sand, slippery even when dry
Riding onto the rock (as some ADV riders do) is technical and best left to experienced riders with a spotter

timings: No formal entry fee is reported for independent visitors; commercial trek groups bundle '~forest permits' into their price, so check locally
Trek is ~5 km round trip, ~2–3 hrs up and down
Start from Bengaluru by ~5 am for sunrise on top; it gets hot and shadeless by late morning
Isha Adiyogi (Avalagurki) is open ~6 am – 8 pm, free entry, with the light show at ~7 pm
cautions: Granite slabs dusted with sand are slippery — wear proper boots for the walk
Locals warn of leopards in the area; avoid going alone or after dark
No water on the trail — carry at least 1.5 litres per person
No drinking or smoking at the temple; carry your litter back
